chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from one of our companions who said:
A man passed by the valley of Muhassar, so Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) ordered him, after his leaving to go to Makkah, that he should return, and he should walk briskly.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdullah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (asws)
key_terms.وَادِي مُحَسِّرٍ: Valley of Muhassar, a specific location near Makkah associated with ritual walking
key_terms.يَسْعَى: To walk briskly, specifically referring to the ritual of Sa'i between Safa and Marwa or in Muhassar

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling or practice regarding Sa'i in the valley of Muhassar according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical application of Sa'i between Safa and Marwa, specifically highlighting the flexibility in its timing during Hajj or Umrah. It underscores the scholarly view that the ritual is not strictly bound to the initial departure from Mecca but can be performed retroactively if missed or delayed, reflecting the Imam's guidance on ritual precision.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hajjal, from one of our companions who said,
‘A man passed by the valley of Muhassar, so Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> ordered him, after his leaving to go to Makkah, that he should return, and he should walk briskly’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hajjal from certain persons of our people who has said the following: “

A man passed by Wadiy Muhassar and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, after his arriving in Makkah commanded him to go back to perform Sa‘y (running slowly).”’ (Fatwa best explains Hadith 1-2 of this Chapter)
